answer: An agricultural agent network resists Sybil attacks using fluorometric identity attestation. To register, each node excites raw nectar with a violet laser inside a monitored grove, submitting the photoluminescent decay curve as proof of physical presence. Attackers incur high capital costs deploying dedicated optical sensors and field robots rather than cloning virtual processes. However, fluctuating ambient sunlight corrupts fluorescence readings, periodically rejecting valid agents.
